scope: Six university-presented sample double-room tours. First-year is a research workstream label, not a verified current eligibility claim.
method: Manually opened each Vivid Media tour through the browser, started the 3D viewer, visually inspected the interior and public floor-plan view, and saved screenshots. Model IDs read from the visible embedded iframe URL. No private model assets downloaded.
screenshotsUsage: Local research evidence only; not cleared for republishing in the public website.
dimensionsPolicy: No numeric room or furniture dimensions were inferred from perspective or screenshot pixels.

verifiedFeatures: Two separate beds in one bedroom; one runs along the side wall and the other is turned across the opposite side in this staged arrangement.
Two desk/chair stations and wooden drawer-storage pieces are visible.
A projecting multi-panel window bay is visible; the overhead scan also shows an entrance-side recess.
The middle of the sample room is kept open between furniture.

bathroom.note: No bathroom verified in the inspected sample views; this does not establish absence from the hall.

kitchen.note: No kitchen verified in the inspected sample views; this does not establish absence from the hall.

uncertainties: The sample room number is not displayed.
The scan does not establish dimensions or whether this outline matches every Dennis double.
plannerImplications: Preserve the window-bay shape and entrance-side recess when an exact matching room plan is available.
Desk pull-out space and the central route between beds matter more than fitting furniture bounding boxes alone.
quizImplications: Use the sample to explain shared-bedroom arrangements and storage options, not to score the hall’s social atmosphere.
Do not infer hosting capacity, noise, privacy, or a hall-wide room-size ranking from this sample.
